# Labeling guide

Hand labels for `npm run eval:extraction`. The definitions below are the exact rubric
the model is given, so disagreements measure the model, not differing definitions.

## How to label

1. Put photos in `images/` (gitignored). One item per photo, plain background if possible.
2. Add one row per photo to `eval/labels.csv`:

   ```
   file,category,color,formality,warmth,seasons
   navy-coat.jpg,outerwear,navy,4,5,fall;winter
   ```

   - `file` is the filename inside `images/`.
   - `seasons` are separated by `;`.
   - Lines starting with `#` are ignored.
3. Label from the photo and this rubric **before** looking at what the model says.
   Pick the closest level; don't leave blanks.

## Rubric

### category
- top: shirts, t-shirts, blouses, sweaters, hoodies, cardigans worn as a main layer
- bottom: trousers, jeans, shorts, skirts
- outerwear: coats, jackets, blazers, rain shells — worn over a top
- shoes: any footwear
- dress: dresses and jumpsuits (replaces both top and bottom)
- accessory: belts, scarves, hats, bags, ties, jewelry

### color
One of: black, white, gray, navy, blue, brown, beige, green, red, pink, purple, yellow, orange, multi.
The single dominant color by visible area. Use 'multi' only when no color covers about half the item (e.g. bold stripes, plaid, florals). Cream/tan/khaki → beige; charcoal → gray; denim blue → blue unless very dark (navy).

### formality (1–5)
- 1: Athletic / lounge — gym wear, sweatpants, slides, graphic hoodies
- 2: Casual — t-shirts, jeans, sneakers, casual shorts
- 3: Smart casual — polos, button-downs, chinos, knit sweaters, clean leather sneakers, loafers
- 4: Business — dress shirts, tailored trousers, blazers, dress shoes, sheath dresses
- 5: Formal — suits, tuxedos, evening gowns, patent dress shoes
Shoes: running/tennis/gym shoes → 1; everyday canvas or casual sneakers → 2; clean minimal leather sneakers, loafers, boat shoes → 3; dress shoes → 4–5.

### warmth (1–5)
- 1: Very light — tank tops, linen, shorts, sandals; for hot weather (above ~80°F / 27°C)
- 2: Light — t-shirts, thin shirts, light dresses, canvas sneakers (~65–80°F / 18–27°C)
- 3: Medium — long sleeves, jeans, light knits, light jackets (~50–65°F / 10–18°C)
- 4: Warm — heavy sweaters, wool trousers, lined jackets, leather boots (~32–50°F / 0–10°C)
- 5: Very warm — parkas, down coats, insulated boots (below ~32°F / 0°C)

### seasons
Any of: spring, summer, fall, winter.
Every season the item is reasonable to wear in. Most items have more than one. A t-shirt is spring/summer/fall; a down parka is winter only; jeans are often all four.
